checked_scope: The complementary-set restriction, finite-election LP equivalence, and determinant bound.
checks: Blocked complementary candidate parts require intersecting strict voter majorities with contradictory a>b and b>a rankings. Taking top choices of ceil(N/2) voters yields a winning set; thus size-k counterexamples need candidates and voters>=2k+1.

For fixed m and blocker assignment, positive common-margin LP feasibility is equivalent to a finite election: forward empirical frequencies and reverse rational optimal vertex/cleared denominators. Zero optimum does not imply strict-majority obstruction; upward closure rules out smaller sets.

At positive-margin vertex with r positive probabilities there are r+1 free variables. At most K+2 relevant active constraints force r<=K+1. After doubling half-integer equations, integer nonsingular matrix entries<=2 have determinant<=(2sqrt(K+2))^(K+2); Cramer gives a common integer voter denominator. This does not bound m or improve the universal3..5 interval.
